note: Content source for the Build Plan page. Edit this; ask Claude to refresh the design from it. status is DONE | NOW | LATER and drives the tile colour, the pill and the sidebar dot. activities[] renders the phase table; notes[] renders the decision log inside the phase; a phase with neither stays a one-line outline row. `lastUpdated` is the date this content last changed. It is provenance for whoever reads this file; the generated pages do NOT render it yet — that lands with the Phase 5 design lock, after which a page behind its source will say so on its face.

site.title: Build Plan
site.lede: Rolling, session-sized. Each phase is timeboxed to about an hour, with an end state you can check.
site.footerNote: Build Plan · rolling. Detailed phases updated after each session from the decisions we make. Prompts: prompts/ · Design: System-Design.html · Backlog: Control-Hub.html.

currentStatus.body: Phases 1–3 complete and the repo is public at github.com/varun-sridharan/aiml-signal-system, with the four HTML surfaces served through GitHub Pages. The Framer runs end to end and its eval harness gates changes to it. Next: Phase 4 — Scout, which replaces the hand-made fixture with real ingested news and is the point the system starts being used rather than designed.

howItWorks: Rolling: the next few phases are detailed; later ones are outlined and filled in as we reach them.
1-hour phases: each phase has an end state and fits one working session.
Milestone activities: each says what it accomplishes and why; the how lives in a canonical prompt under prompts/ (final & holistic — see the folder README).
Notes = decision log: Claude maintains the decisions, tradeoffs, and priorities per phase from our sessions, and updates them when a phase concludes.
Content vs design: every document is JSON content rendered by a design from Claude Design. Claude edits the JSON; the HTML is generated and never hand-edited.

Rituals: end of session — Claude updates the concepts reference JSON and reminds you to refresh it. End of phase — Claude reminds you to regenerate all static docs whose JSON changed (concepts, plan, design record), since a phase boundary always moves the plan and the decision log.

phases.title: First commit & the Claude Code loop
phases.endState: all scaffolding committed & pushed to GitHub via a Claude Code session you drove yourself.
phases.why: your work becomes versioned and accessible anywhere, and you learn the core approve-edits loop on a low-stakes task before building agents.

activities.outcome: You see how it reads the codebase before editing
activities.why: Builds trust in what it will change

activities.outcome: README describes the project + real folder structure
activities.why: Entry point for you and, later, the public

notes: Repo stays private now; when exposed later, exclude Control-Hub.html + data/ from the public build (personal telemetry).
Deliberately low-stakes (README + commit) to learn the CLI loop before touching agents.
Done 2026-08-09: committed as e1661d7, pushed to origin/main, generated with Opus 5.
Claude Code added .DS_Store to .gitignore (macOS junk) — one change beyond prompt scope, flagged transparently. Environment hygiene, not a code decision.
Confirmed the pages don't read data/ yet (content inline) — wiring deferred to Phases 6 & 9, as designed.

phases.title: Build & prove the Framer
phases.endState: a Framer agent that turns data/evals/golden/reference_2026-08-04.json into a brief matching the Bento reference voice.
phases.why: Framer quality is the riskiest assumption in the system — if the voice lands, the whole thing is worth building; it's the cheapest bet to de-risk first.

activities.activity: Finalize the Framer build prompt (+ Evals)
activities.outcome: Canonical prompt with faithfulness/usefulness graders baked in
activities.why: Reproducible recipe; evals from day one

activities.activity: Generate the Framer agent via Claude Code

activities.outcome: You judge whether the voice sounds right
activities.why: The go / no-go on the whole system
activities.prompt: — your taste is the gate

notes: Locked Framer rules: worked examples on AI items only; synthesis "thread" required; DO THIS reserved for AI; reading-time header; inline connections.
Faithfulness = hard zero-hallucination gate (objective); usefulness = soft, learned target (subjective).
Test against application/Signal.html, not vibes.
Done 2026-08-09 (commit df8adfd, Opus 5): Framer built & run — 7 items, 2 DO THIS, ~5 min read, $0.10. Batched to 2 calls (Opus framing + Haiku check) with prompt caching + cost breaker, all working.

Voice verdict = GO: thread carries a real correlation + contradiction and reaches its own conclusion; connections genuine. Two weak spots to tune later: iStar example clause doesn't parse; Kimi K3 example vaguer than the reference's concrete "~1/10th cost".

Key finding → Phase 3: the faithfulness check produced a false positive (flagged $965B as unsupported though it was in the excerpt). Two grader bugs: it missed a clause, and it graded thread/headline text against a single item's excerpt. The grader needs its own eval; the thread must be checked against the union of excerpts.
Deviations, both fine: built the prompt file fresh (option 3, no invented Scout list); switched the framing call to streaming after the SDK blocked a 24k-token non-streaming request (no spend).

phases.title: Framer eval harness (golden set)
phases.endState: a tiny offline eval that scores the Framer (faithfulness assertion + usefulness rubric) against 1–2 labeled days.
phases.why: turns "is the voice right?" from a vibe into a number, and makes every future prompt tweak safe via regression.

activities.activity: Build a golden set from labeled days

activities.outcome: Grader rewritten: claim ledger with quoted spans, correct scope, code-verified evidence

activities.why: Safe iteration on the Framer prompt

notes: Eval harness lives in the repo from early on; the Tuner-driven learning matures later (needs weeks of data).
Held-out slice kept separate from anything the Tuner adapts on (train/test hygiene).
First golden-set case comes free: the Phase 2 grader false positive. Fix the check to (a) not miss clauses and (b) grade the thread against the union of all item excerpts, not one item's.

Done 2026-08-19 (Opus 5): run_evals.py runs three checks — faithfulness (hard gate, 1 Haiku call), structural assertions (hard gate, free), usefulness rubric (soft, reported). Both seeded regressions pass; run costs ~$0.02.

The grader's real bug was scope, not carelessness. It was shown the excerpt first and the writing second, so it enumerated the excerpt's claims and never checked the framing at all — which is why $965B "failed" and why fabricated facts sailed through. Writing now comes first in the payload, the excerpt is labelled ground truth, and each claim must carry a verbatim span.
Second false positive found while labelling: the 2026-08-13 re-run flagged "~80% of Q1 dollars", which the excerpt states word for word. Seeded as a second regression case.

Two extras beyond the brief, both earned by a failing test: a code check that every quoted span is literally in the excerpt (a grader can invent a citation; a substring match can't), and temperature=0 on the grader — at default sampling it disagreed with itself on ~1 run in 3, which would have failed builds at random. 5/5 clean runs after.

Known limit, carried to Phase 8: the gate is deterministic per input, but on unseen days the grader still sometimes enumerates an inference as a claim. Fine for regression (the golden day is fixed); revisit before the grader guards live briefs — likely by moving it to a stronger model.
Usefulness stays ungated until calibrated against your own ratings. Judge runs on Haiku to keep spend low; upgrade it the day it starts gating.

phases.title: Scout — seed sources + fetch
phases.endState: Scout pulls candidate items from the fixed seed list into data/.
phases.why: turns on real intake so the Framer runs on live items, not a sample.

phases.title: Gatekeeper basics + Suppressed drawer · design lock
phases.endState: provenance + corroboration + dedup filtering, with everything killed logged to the Suppressed drawer. Also: a volume guard — the Gatekeeper caps how many items reach the Framer, and the Framer asserts loudly on item count rather than silently truncating. And the design lock: Signal.html and Control-Hub.html are live surfaces whose content changes daily, so their design must be finalised here — Claude Design delivers a renderer with a data slot, not a regenerated page, and after this point the visuals stop changing while the agents feed it. Templates must also render lastUpdated from the content JSON, so a page that is behind its source says so on its face instead of relying on memory.
phases.why: kills noise and gives you the false-negative audit trail that keeps FOMO dead. The volume guard protects the Framer's single-call design — a 60-item day means the Gatekeeper failed, and should fail loudly rather than drop items. The design lock has to land before Phase 6 wiring: you can't regenerate a page in a design tool every morning, so the live surfaces need a fixed template the pipeline writes into.

phases.title: Daily loop end-to-end (News renders from data/)
phases.endState: a real daily brief generated Scout→Gatekeeper→Framer→News.html, with quiet-day behavior. Plus three closures found during the Phase 3 walkthrough: (1) retry loop — the Framer regenerates a flagged item and re-checks before writing, instead of flagging and shipping anyway; (2) daily smoke test — run the free structural checks on each day's output so contract violations surface immediately, not at the next prompt edit; (3) eval regenerate mode — optionally re-run the Framer on the golden input so a Framer prompt change is regression-tested, not just the grader.
phases.why: the anti-FOMO daily value goes live — you start using it every morning. The three closures turn "flagged" into "fixed", catch drift the day it happens, and close the gap that today's harness only regression-tests the grader, never the writer.

phases.title: Coach — standalone homework
phases.endState: a weekly 60-min exercise generated from the week's items, written to the backlog.
phases.why: turns reading into doing (job b), before the harder repo-grounding step.

phases.title: Coach — repo grounding
phases.endState: homework that fits a real spot in your repos, verified by assertions against the code.
phases.why: the magic feature — and the highest hallucination risk, so it comes after trust is built.

phases.title: Control Room live (metrics.json)
phases.endState: the Control Room renders real eval metrics, pending actions, and elicitation questions — plus the front-door Orchestrator goes live (routes user actions: add-source → Scout, question → chat, feedback/intent → Tuner; the one live-API agent).
phases.why: closes the report→elicit→label loop so the system can improve deliberately.

phases.title: Tuner — learned personalization
phases.endState: source reputation + topic priors that adapt from your feedback, with the diversity guardrail.
phases.why: the system starts getting better at you — but only after weeks of data exist.

phases.title: Commercial prep (documented)
phases.endState: shared-base / per-user split proven; auth + multi-tenant scoped when/if productizing.
phases.why: the path from personal system to product, kept open by the user_id seam.

crossCutting.title: Cross-cutting infrastructure
crossCutting.note: A trajectory, not a single phase.
items: Data layer: JSON files now → SQLite when history/queries get awkward (~Phase 6–9) → Postgres + pgvector incl. auth sessions at multi-tenant (Phase 11). The user_id seam keeps the migration mechanical.
Observability: extend usage.json into a structured per-run trace now → an LLM-observability tool at deploy (~Phase 6+).
Cost tracker: ledger + circuit-breaker exist now → Control Room charts it live in Phase 9.
